title: How many matchsticks make w squares in a row?
description: Squares in a row are made from matchsticks. The first square needs four matchsticks and every new square adds three, which gives thirty one for ten squares and three w plus one for w squares.
teaching_notes: One idea: the first square is special and every later square adds three, so w squares have w minus one later squares. Watch for students who write three w or four w.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of the bracket formula: the first picture is counted once and the later pictures add the same amount, written with a bracket and then opened.
video_script.substitution: The method of three plus two times the bracket y minus one, with four plus three times the bracket w minus one for squares in a row.
video_script.anchor: a row of squares made from matchsticks
video_script.payoff_line: Ten squares need thirty one matchsticks, and w squares need three w plus one

final_answer.value: 31 matchsticks for 10 squares, and 4 + 3(w − 1) = 3w + 1 for w squares
final_answer.spoken: thirty one matchsticks for ten squares, and three w plus one for w squares

hold_back: Answer: 31 matchsticks for 10 squares, and 4 + 3(w − 1) = 3w + 1 for w squares
never_show: the finished formula before the answer beat
maths_rules: one square needs 4 matchsticks; each new square joined to the row adds 3
video_script.design: One idea: four for the first square, and three more for each later square. Assumes the example of a count with a bracket. The row of squares stays on the stage.
open_questions: The picture is not in the extracted book text; the video follows the worklist: 4 for the first square and 3 for each square joined after it.

narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We find the matchsticks for ten squares, and then for w squares. We work the same way as the example in your book.

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>First, ten squares are the first square and nine more squares.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>The matchsticks are four plus three times nine, which is four plus twenty seven. That is thirty one.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: w squares: the first square and (w − 1) more, so 4 + 3(w − 1)

marks.s2a: w squares are split into the first square and w − 1 more

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Second, w squares are the first square and w minus one more squares.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>The matchsticks are four plus three times the bracket w minus one.
<bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, open the bracket. Three times the bracket w minus one is three w minus three.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Four minus three is one, so the matchsticks are three w plus one.

marks.s4b: 31 is matched to the count for ten squares

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Fourth, check with w as ten. Three times ten plus one is thirty one.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>This matches the count we made for ten squares.
